sources.note: Bootstrapping WebSockets with HTTP/2 - single-stream upgrade over HTTP/2, and the RFC 6455 reference. Useful for upgrade-transcript mechanics; the abstract was too thin to cite for any specific evidence claim.
WebSocket.close() reference. Fetched and verified reachable but the fetched text is mostly MDN navigation chrome; no quotable prose survived de-tagging.
WebSocket.send() reference. Reachable; body de-tags to navigation plus a signature list, so no candidate evidence span extracted from it.
WebSocket.protocol property. Reachable; the subprotocol field is relevant to origin confusion research but yielded no citable prose span.
WebSocket.binaryType property. Reachable; descriptor text is too thin for an evidence quote.
Socket.IO server middleware reference. Confirms the allowRequest-style origin gate exists as a first-class knob; too terse to cite.
MDN Origin header reference. Reachable, but the prose section de-tags to navigation and the status-code table; only the RFC 6454 origin-concept text was citable.
MDN cookie guide. Reachable and on-topic for cookie scope and SameSite, but the Set-Cookie reference already carried the citable spans.
MDN setRequestHeader reference. Confirms a custom header forces a preflight (the reason a header-based CSRF token is not reachable from a simple cross-origin form); no citable span extracted.
MDN form submit reference. Useful corroboration that a form submission reaches the server cross-origin; prose too thin to cite.
MDN fetch() reference. Reachable; the credentials material found was error-path prose rather than the SameSite/credentials semantics needed.
HTTP/1.1 Semantics and Content. Reachable; Origin-header discussion is spread across sections in a way the phrase search did not isolate cleanly.

WSTG CSRF test section. URL resolves 200 but the fetch returns the WSTG foreword and full table of contents instead of the CSRF section body - a fetch-extraction problem, not a dead page. Every wstg.owasp.org deep path for this section returned 404.
RFC 2104 HMAC. Reachable and relevant to HMAC-based CSRF token design; no candidate evidence span for this wave's claims.
CWE-346 Origin Validation Error - the obvious CSRF companion to CWE-1275, but this URL is already cited in db/sources.json, so it was not reusable.
Node v8 serialization API - v8.serialize/v8.deserialize. Cited once for the deserialize entry point; the page's format detail is signature-level only, so most of it remains unused.
PHP serialize(). Reachable; pairs with the unserialize() page but adds no independent evidence span beyond it.

PHP stream wrappers. Reachable and highly relevant to SSRF via wrapper abuse (file://, gopher-style handler selection); page de-tags to a wrapper table without quotable prose on the security implications.
CWE-470 Unsafe Reflection. Cited twice for deser; its parent-class framing means further reflection items will exhaust it.
CWE-1123 Lack of Protection against Reverse Engineering. Verified reachable but off-target for the deserialization class.
CWE-1327 Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address. Verified reachable; off-target for deser, relevant to ssrf/auth.
CAPEC-137 Parameter Injection. Reachable; sibling to object injection but not cited here since CWE-470 carries the claim.
CAPEC-502 Intent Spoof. Verified reachable but is an Android intent-spoofing pattern, unrelated to serialization deserialization.
CAPEC-586 Object Injection. Reachable at only ~5KB, which is near the tool's refusal threshold; body de-tags to the pattern summary with no substantive mechanics.
Obsolete RFC 7159 JSON. Reachable; superseded by RFC 8259, which carried the same quotable abstract, so kept only as a historical pointer.
TLS 1.3. Verified reachable; off-target for deserialization.

Node fs API. Reachable at ~260KB; the file-open flags section documents exclusive-create semantics relevant to TOCTOU on local files, but nothing citable was needed once Redis and CWE covered the mechanism.
Python threading module. Reachable; documents locks as the mutual-exclusion answer, i.e. the mitigation side rather than an observation a reviewer can re-check.
SET command, including its NX/XX conditional options. The natural corroboration for a compare-and-set disproof; the transactions page already carried the citable check-and-set span.
INCR command. Reachable; the atomic-integer-counter alternative to the lost-update pattern, but the text de-tags largely to embedded command metadata JSON.

DynamoDB condition expressions - conditional writes as a compare-and-set. URL returns 200 but only ~11KB of breadcrumb/nav; the ConditionalCheckFailed behaviour needed for a disproof was not in the fetched text.

Apache mod_proxy reference. Reachable at ~76KB; documents the forwarding proxy behaviour that underlies CWE-441, but as generic module prose it does not make a sharper evidence claim than the OWASP API page.
nginx stream proxy module. Reachable; TCP-layer forwarding rather than HTTP fetching, so it is a weaker SSRF witness than the HTTP-layer sources already cited.
nginx http upstream module. Reachable; server-selection and keepalive behaviour only, not an SSRF witness.
Tomcat valve configuration. Reachable at ~95KB; RemoteIpValve and similar are about the opposite direction (trusting forwarded headers), so useful mainly as a counter-example source.
